questions.question: Which property of an element is inversely related to its ionisation energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atomic radius**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ionisation energy** is the energy required to remove an electron from an atom in its gaseous state.
 
• The **atomic radius** is the distance from the nucleus of an atom to the outermost electron shell.
 
• As the **atomic radius** increases, the attraction between the nucleus and the electrons decreases.
 
• This decreased attraction makes it easier to remove an electron, resulting in lower **ionisation energy**.
 
• Therefore, there is an **inverse relationship** between the atomic radius and ionisation energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electronegativity**__

 __
 
• **Electronegativity** is a measure of an atom's ability to attract and hold onto electrons.
 
• Elements with high electronegativity have a strong attraction for electrons.
 
• Typically, electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group in the periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Atomic mass**__
 __
 
• **Atomic mass** is the mass of an atom, usually expressed in atomic mass units (amu).
 
• It is approximately equivalent to the number of protons and neutrons in the atom (mass number).
 
• Atomic mass does not have a direct relationship with ionisation energy.
 
 
 
• **Electron affinity**__
 
 
• **Electron affinity** is the energy change that occurs when an electron is added to a neutral atom in the gaseous state.
 
• It is generally exothermic, meaning energy is released when an electron is added.
 
• Elements with high electron affinity values are more likely to gain electrons.

questions.question: In which year did the Government of India pass the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2005**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)** was passed by the **Government of India** in the year **2005**.
 
• It aims to enhance the livelihood security of people in **rural areas** by guaranteeing at least **100 days of wage-employment** in a financial year to every household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
 
• MGNREGA is a social security measure that provides a legal guarantee for employment.
 
• The Act was passed under the leadership of the then Prime Minister, **Dr. Manmohan Singh**, and was a significant step towards poverty alleviation.
 
• It is considered one of the largest and most ambitious social welfare programs in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• MGNREGA is monitored by the **Ministry of Rural Development**, Government of India.
 
• The Act has provisions for ensuring **transparency and accountability** in the implementation of the scheme.
 
• It involves the **Gram Panchayats** in planning and implementing the works.
 
• Funds for the scheme are shared between the Central and State Governments.

questions.question:
Find the odd one out.

Vacuoles, Nucleus, Ribosomes, Lysosomes
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ribosomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes** are the odd one out because they are not membrane-bound organelles, unlike the other options.
 
• Ribosomes are involved in **protein synthesis** and are found either floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• They are composed of **ribosomal RNA (rRNA)** and proteins.
 
• The primary function of ribosomes is to translate messenger RNA (mRNA) into proteins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nucleus**__

 __
 
• The **nucleus** is a membrane-bound organelle that contains the cell's genetic material (DNA).
 
• It controls cellular activities by regulating gene expression.
 
• The nucleus is surrounded by the **nuclear envelope**, which has pores to allow the exchange of materials.
 
 
 
• **Vacuoles**__
 __
 
• **Vacuoles** are membrane-bound organelles found in plant and fungal cells, and some protist, animal, and bacterial cells.
 
• They are responsible for the storage of nutrients, waste products, and maintaining turgor pressure in plant cells.
 
• In animal cells, vacuoles are generally smaller and more numerous.
 
 
 
• **Lysosomes**__
 
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound organelles containing digestive enzymes.
 
• They break down excess or worn-out cell parts, and can be involved in destroying invading viruses and bacteria.
 
• Lysosomes are often called the "stomach" of the cell due to their role in digestion.

questions.question: What is the main objective of zero-based budgeting?

options.text: To assess the effectiveness of each programme and activity with the output
Establishing a relationship between inputs and outputs
Examining the objectives for which funds are provided
Re-evaluation of all the activities every year when budget provisions are made

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Re-evaluation of all the activities every year when budget provisions are made**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zero-based budgeting (ZBB)** is a budgeting method where all expenses must be justified for each new period.
 
• In ZBB, every function within an organization is analyzed for its needs and costs.
 
• The primary objective is the **re-evaluation of all activities annually**, ensuring that funds are allocated efficiently.
 
• It starts from a "zero base" and every function is reviewed comprehensively.
 
• This method encourages cost management and helps in identifying and eliminating unnecessary expenditures.
 
• ZBB is used to allocate resources based on the necessity and efficiency of projects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **To assess the effectiveness of each programme and activity with the output**__

 __
 
• This option pertains to **performance budgeting** where the focus is on outcomes and outputs of programs.
 
• Performance budgeting links funds allocated to measurable results.
 
 
 
• **Establishing a relationship between inputs and outputs**__
 __
 
• This approach is often seen in **output budgeting** or **performance-based budgeting**.
 
• It focuses on efficiency by examining how inputs (resources) are converted into outputs (services).
 
 
 
• **Examining the objectives for which funds are provided**__
 
 
• This option is related to **program budgeting**, which allocates funds according to the objectives of each program.
 
• Program budgeting aims to allocate resources based on programs' goals and objectives.

questions.question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is taken from the USA's constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Removal of Supreme Court Judges**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Removal of Supreme Court Judges** is a feature of the Indian Constitution adopted from the **USA's Constitution**.
 
• The process involves an **impeachment procedure** which is quite similar to that in the United States.
 
• The **President** of India can remove a Supreme Court judge only after an address by the Parliament which is supported by a majority of the total membership of each House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of the House present and voting.
 
• This process ensures the **independence of the judiciary** from the executive and legislative branches of the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Parliamentary Privileges**__

 __
 
• **Parliamentary Privileges** refer to the special rights, immunities, and exemptions enjoyed by the two Houses of Parliament, their committees, and their members.
 
• These privileges are based on the **British parliamentary system**.
 
 
 
• **Prerogative Writs**__
 __
 
• **Prerogative Writs**, like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari, are judicial orders that command the performance of a specific act or duty.
 
• This concept is borrowed from the **British legal system**.
 
 
 
• **Cabinet System**__
 
 
• The **Cabinet System** of government, also known as the Westminster system, includes the role of the Prime Minister and a cabinet of ministers.
 
• This system is derived from the **United Kingdom**.

questions.question: The layer made up of unconsolidated rock, dust, soil, etc. that is deposited on a bed rock surface like a blanket is known as
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Regolith**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Regolith** is a layer of loose, heterogeneous material covering solid rock.
 
• This layer includes **dust, soil, broken rock, and other related materials**.
 
• It is found on **Earth, the Moon, Mars, and some other celestial bodies**.
 
• The term **regolith** is derived from the Greek words "rhegos" (blanket) and "lithos" (rock).
 
• On Earth, regolith plays a significant role in **soil formation** and can be an essential factor in **ecosystem dynamics**.
 
• It also acts as a medium for **plant growth** and serves as a repository for **groundwater**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Talus**__

 __
 
• **Talus** refers to a pile of rock debris that accumulates at the base of a cliff, chute, or slope.
 
• It is typically formed by the mechanical weathering of rocks, such as through freeze-thaw processes.
 
 
 
• **Scree**__
 __
 
• **Scree** is a collection of broken rock fragments at the base of crags, mountain cliffs, or valley shoulders.
 
• Scree often forms through the action of gravitational forces.
 
 
 
• **Protolith**__
 
 
• **Protolith** is the original, unmetamorphosed rock from which a given metamorphic rock is formed.
 
• Identifying a protolith is essential in understanding the history and conditions of metamorphism.

questions.question: In December 2022, the Parliament passed the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill, 2022. This bill aims to make use of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**non-fossil fuels**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill, 2022, aims to promote the use of **non-fossil fuels** to ensure a sustainable and environmentally friendly energy supply.
 
• The bill seeks to encourage the adoption of **renewable energy sources** such as solar, wind, biomass, and hydrogen.
 
• This legislative move is in line with India's commitment to reduce its **carbon footprint** and tackle **climate change**.
 
• By shifting towards non-fossil fuels, the government aims to reduce dependency on **imported fossil fuels** and promote **energy security**.
 
• The bill also includes provisions for the establishment of a **carbon market** and the imposition of energy consumption standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tungsten filament bulbs in houses**__

 __
 
• Tungsten filament bulbs are an older technology and are being phased out in favor of more energy-efficient lighting such as **LED bulbs**.
 
• These bulbs consume more **electricity** compared to modern lighting solutions and are not aligned with energy conservation goals.
 
 
 
• **Subsidy on petrol vehicles**__
 __
 
• Providing subsidies on petrol vehicles would **increase the consumption of fossil fuels** and is contrary to the objectives of promoting sustainability and reducing carbon emissions.
 
 
 
• **Electric vehicles**__
 
 
• While promoting electric vehicles (EVs) is essential for reducing emissions, the bill specifically focuses on the broader category of **non-fossil fuels**, which includes renewable energy sources.

questions.question: Which of the following places in India receive the highest rainfall?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Mawsynram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mawsynram** is a village in the **East Khasi Hills district** of Meghalaya, India.
 
• It holds the record for being the **wettest place on Earth** with an average annual rainfall of about **11,871 millimeters** (467.4 inches).
 
• The heavy rainfall is mainly due to the **geographical location** and the presence of the **Bay of Bengal branch of the Indian monsoon.**
 
• The region's **topography** and **wind patterns** contribute to the high precipitation.
 
• Rainfall in Mawsynram is caused by the **orographic lift**, where moist air rises over the hills and cools down to release rain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Patna**__

 __
 
• **Patna** is the capital city of **Bihar** state in India.
 
• It is located on the southern bank of the **Ganges River**.
 
• Patna experiences a **humid subtropical climate** with moderate rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Guwahati**__
 __
 
• **Guwahati** is a major city in the **northeastern state of Assam**, India.
 
• It lies on the southern bank of the **Brahmaputra River**.
 
• Guwahati has a **tropical monsoon climate** and receives substantial rainfall but not as much as Mawsynram.
 
 
 
• **Imphal**__
 
 
• **Imphal** is the capital city of the **northeastern state of Manipur**, India.
 
• The city is situated in the **Imphal Valley**.
 
• Imphal has a **subtropical climate** with moderate to high rainfall, especially during the monsoon season.

questions.question: Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma is credited with single-handedly popularising which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Santoor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma** is credited with single-handedly popularising the **Santoor**.
 
• The **Santoor** is a traditional **Indian musical instrument** that originates from **Kashmir**.
 
• The instrument is typically played with a pair of light wooden mallets and has a distinct, melodious sound.
 
• Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma modified the **Santoor** to suit the requirements of classical Indian music.
 
• His innovative playing techniques and compositions brought the **Santoor** to the forefront of Indian classical music.
 
• He is also known for his collaborations with other renowned musicians and his contributions to Indian film music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sarod**__

 __
 
• The **Sarod** is a stringed instrument used mainly in **Indian classical music**.
 
• It is known for its deep, weighty, introspective sound.
 
• Prominent Sarod players include **Ustad Amjad Ali Khan** and **Ali Akbar Khan**.
 
 
 
• **Sitar**__
 __
 
• The **Sitar** is another popular stringed instrument in Indian classical music.
 
• It has a long neck and a gourd resonating chamber, and it is played with a plectrum.
 
• **Ravi Shankar** and **Vilayat Khan** are some of the most famous Sitar players.
 
 
 
• **Tabla**__
 
 
• The **Tabla** is a pair of twin hand drums from the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It is the most important percussion instrument in Hindustani classical music.
 
• Notable Tabla players include **Zakir Hussain** and **Alla Rakha**.

questions.question: In a Parliamentary system, who among the following is known as the head of the Government?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Prime Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the head of the Government in a parliamentary system.
 
• He or she is responsible for running the **government** and implementing its policies and decisions.
 
• The Prime Minister is the leader of the **executive branch** of the government.
 
• He or she is appointed by the **President** but must have the support of the **majority** in the **lower house of Parliament**.
 
• The Prime Minister selects and leads a team of **ministers** who are responsible for specific government departments.
 
• In countries like **India and the United Kingdom**, the Prime Minister holds the most powerful political office.
 
• The Prime Minister represents the **country** in various international forums and meetings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chief Minister**__

 __
 
• The **Chief Minister** is the head of the government at the **state level** in countries like **India**.
 
• He or she functions similarly to the Prime Minister but within a specific state.
 
• The Chief Minister is appointed by the **Governor** of the state.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice**__
 __
 
• The **Chief Justice** is the head of the **judiciary** and the highest-ranking judge in a court system.
 
• In India, the Chief Justice of India heads the **Supreme Court**.
 
 
 
• **President**__
 
 
• The **President** is the **head of state** and represents the country ceremonially.
 
• In a parliamentary system, the President's role is more **ceremonial** and less involved in daily government operations.

questions.question: In the year 1946, a three-tiered confederation for transfer of power to India was proposed by the ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Cabinet Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Cabinet Mission** was a group of high-ranking members from the British government sent to India in **1946**.
 
• Its primary objective was to discuss and plan for the transfer of power from British rule to Indian leadership.
 
• The Mission proposed a **three-tiered confederation** consisting of provinces grouped into three sections: **Group A (Hindus majority provinces), Group B (Muslim majority provinces), and Group C (the princely states)**.
 
• This structure aimed to address the interests of various groups and provide a framework for a united yet flexible governance system.
 
• The Cabinet Mission's plan was ultimately rejected by the Muslim League, leading to further negotiations and eventually the partition of India in **1947**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Regulating Act**__

 __
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** was the first attempt by the British government to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.
 
• It established a system of dual control, with both the company and the British government involved in administration.
 
• This act marked the beginning of British parliamentary control over India.
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Act**__
 __
 
• The **Rowlatt Act**, also known as the **Black Act**, was passed in 1919 by the British Government in India.
 
• It allowed the government to imprison any person suspected of terrorism without trial for up to two years.
 
• This act led to widespread anger and protests, including the infamous Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
 
 
• **Simon Commission**__
 
 
• The **Simon Commission** was a group of seven British Members of Parliament that was sent to India in 1927 to study constitutional reform.
 
• It was met with strong opposition from Indian leaders because it did not include any Indian members.
 
• The slogan "**Simon Go Back**" was popular during the protests against the commission.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Alpasi Festival celebrated annually, where a holy bath of the deities in the sea is the primary attraction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT related to Macaulay?

options.text: He considered Indian and Arab literature inferior to the Western literature.
He believed that India is an uncivilised country which needs to be taught the lessons of civilisation.
He strongly advocated giving English language education to Indians.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Macaulay was an orientalist scholar.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thomas Babington Macaulay** was a British historian and politician.
 
• He is best known for his role in introducing English education in India.
 
• **Macaulay** is famous for his "Minute on Indian Education" of 1835, which advocated for the promotion of English language education in India.
 
• He believed that English education was superior and that it would help civilize and modernize Indian society.
 
• Macaulay viewed Indian and Arab literature as inferior to Western literature, reflecting his Eurocentric perspective.
 
• He did not support orientalism, which is the appreciation and study of Asian cultures, languages, and histories.
 
• Instead, he promoted Western education and ideas as a means to reform and develop India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Orientalism**__

 __
 
• **Orientalism** refers to the study and appreciation of Asian cultures, languages, and histories.
 
• Orientalists were scholars who advocated for the preservation and study of Eastern traditions and knowledge.
 
• Macaulay was not an orientalist; he opposed the idea of promoting traditional Indian education and languages.
 
 
 
• **English Education in India**__
 
 
• Macaulay's efforts led to the establishment of English as the medium of instruction in Indian schools and colleges.
 
• He believed that Western education would help create a class of Indians who could assist in governing the country and spreading Western values.
 
• This policy had a lasting impact on the Indian education system and the use of the English language in India.

questions.question: When was the National Digital Communications Policy launched in India?

• This policy aimed at providing **broadband** for all, creating **4 million jobs** in the digital communications sector, and enhancing the contribution of the digital communications sector to **8% of India's GDP**.
 
• The policy envisions ensuring **universal broadband connectivity** at 50 Mbps to every citizen.
 
• It focuses on providing 1 Gbps connectivity to all **Gram Panchayats** by 2020 and 10 Gbps by 2022.
 
• One of its key missions is to propel India to the top 50 nations in the **ICT Development Index** of the International Telecommunication Union.
 
• It also aims to attract investments worth **USD 100 billion** in the digital communications sector.
 
• The policy promotes innovation and startup ecosystems in the digital communication sector.

• The policy addresses the need for enhancing the coverage of **broadband** and increasing the speed of internet services across the country.
 
• It aims at developing a **robust digital infrastructure** to support the vision of a digital-first economy.
 
• The policy emphasizes the importance of **emerging technologies** like 5G, IoT (Internet of Things), and AI (Artificial Intelligence) in driving economic growth.
 
• It also focuses on ensuring digital **sovereignty** and security by promoting **indigenous manufacturing** and establishing a comprehensive data protection regime.

questions.question: Pellagra is a deficiency disease that usually occurs due to lack of which of the following nutrients?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Niacin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pellagra** is a deficiency disease caused by a lack of **Niacin** (Vitamin B3) in the diet.
 
• Niacin is essential for the body as it helps in the **metabolism of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins**.
 
• Deficiency of Niacin can lead to the "three Ds" - **Dermatitis, Diarrhea, and Dementia**, and if left untreated, can be fatal.
 
• Niacin can be obtained from foods such as **meat, fish, poultry, and whole grains**.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the body's production of **energy** and in the maintenance of **healthy skin and nerves**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vitamin E**__

 __
 
• **Vitamin E** is a powerful **antioxidant** that helps protect cells from damage.
 
• It is essential for **immune function**, skin health, and eye health.
 
• Rich sources include **nuts, seeds, and green leafy vegetables**.
 
 
 
• **Iodine**__
 __
 
• **Iodine** is crucial for the production of **thyroid hormones** which regulate metabolism.
 
• A deficiency can lead to **goiter and hypothyroidism**.
 
• Sources include **iodized salt, seafood, and dairy products**.
 
 
 
• **Riboflavin**__
 
 
• **Riboflavin** (Vitamin B2) is important for **energy production** and the metabolism of fats, drugs, and steroids.
 
• Deficiency can cause **mouth sores, sore throat, and skin disorders**.
 
• Found in **eggs, milk, green vegetables, and fortified cereals**.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers introduced the 'jharokha darshan' in the Mughal dynasty?

• **Jharokha Darshan** was a tradition started by **Akbar**, the third Mughal emperor.
 
• This practice involved the emperor appearing before his subjects from a **balcony** (jharokha) of his palace every morning.
 
• The purpose was to **connect with the common people** and assure them of his presence and involvement in their lives.
 
• The practice also had a **political motive** to reinforce the divine status of the emperor, reflecting the belief that the king was a representative of God on earth.
 
• It was a **means of communication** without intermediaries, helping to establish a direct bond between the emperor and his subjects.

• He faced setbacks and was temporarily ousted from India by **Sher Shah Suri**.
 
 
 
• **Shahjahan**__

• His reign is often considered the **golden age of Mughal architecture**.
